claim: Schoenfeld's belief list includes the '5 minutes or less' belief; students surveyed named typical homework problem times of about 2 min (mean 2.2, n=221) and gave up on 'impossible' problems after about 12 min (mean 11.7, n=227). Numbers come via Schoenfeld's own reviews; only secondary reading.
agent_test: Compare agent give-up point (tokens before declaring impossible) with and without an explicit 'hard problems take long' note at equal total tokens.

claim: Schoenfeld's wild goose chase count, from the primary 1982 NSF final report: 7 of 12 pretest protocols (58%, six student pairs x two problems) were Reading/Exploration with no progress control, vs 2 of 12 (17%) after a month-long problem-solving course. Unit is protocols; no test statistic for this count; author-coded; no independent replication found. In the same report the course group's problem test mean went 21 to 73 vs control 14 to 24 (interaction F(1,17)=48.2, p<.001).
agent_test: Count unreviewed commitments to one approach in traces; add a forced progress check every N tokens and compare solve rate.

claim: Math anxiety correlates negatively with math performance at about r=-.27 to -.34 across meta-analyses (Hembree -.27, Ma -.34, Caviola -.30 [-.32,-.28], I2=98%). Working-memory mediation is negligible (indirect B<=.05).
agent_test: Not directly testable; causal direction also unsettled (Carey 2016).

claim: Growth-mindset interventions have tiny effects on achievement: Macnamara and Burgoyne 0.05 overall, 0.02 in best-evidence studies; Sisk d=0.08; yet Yeager's national study found +0.10 grade points in lower achievers. Contested, heterogeneous, small.
agent_test: Skip; humans-only. Use only as a warning against effect-size inflation in belief claims.

claim: Emotional appeals in prompts (EmotionPrompt) raise benchmark scores: +8.00% relative on Instruction Induction, +115% on BIG-Bench (large relative because base scores are low); human study 106 participants +10.9%. Effect varies by stimulus and can shrink when stimuli are stacked. The paper's zero-shot vs few-shot comparison (0.33 vs 2.05) is stated ambiguously. Gap search: a conceptual replication on newer models found no significant gain (overall +1%, chi2=0.11, p=.74; best single +8.7%, p=.16) and recomputed the original average-of-stimuli gain as 4.42% on BIG-Bench and 2.58% overall, not 115% (best of 11 stimuli). A 2026 test on Qwen3, Llama 3.3 and DeepSeek-V3.2 found GSM8K stays within about 2 pp of baseline.
schema_part: none (prompt tone; section 4b not to add)
agent_test: Replicate at equal tokens on a math set with a length-matched neutral sentence; the extra words may be the effect.

claim: Negative or stress-style prompts (NegativePrompt) also raise scores (+12.89% Instruction Induction, +46.25% BIG-Bench), and OPRO found 'Take a deep breath' scored 80.2 vs 71.8 for 'Let's think step by step' on PaLM 2-L GSM8K; wording effects are real but model-specific, not about affect per se.
agent_test: Run a phrase sweep on our model; expect model-specific, non-transferable results.

claim: Anxiety narratives raise LLM questionnaire anxiety scores (STICSA higher for all robust LLMs); mindfulness text lowers it (STAI about 77 to 44). This shows self-report shifts, not that math reasoning changes.
agent_test: Measure math accuracy after anxiety vs neutral pre-prompts; do not assume the questionnaire shift transfers.

claim: Intrinsic self-correction by prompting does not help and often hurts reasoning: GPT-3.5 CommonSenseQA 75.8 to 38.1; GPT-4 GSM8K 95.5 to 89.0 over rounds. Gains appear only with external feedback or oracle labels (GPT-3.5 GSM8K 95.5 with oracle).
schema_part: G (no unverified self-revision), O (verify with tools)
agent_test: Compare revise-on-own-judgement vs revise-only-on-verifier-signal at equal tokens.

claim: Models cave under social pressure: 'Are you sure?' drops accuracy up to 27% (Claude 1.3), answer changes 32% (GPT-4) to 86% (Claude 1.3), false admission 42% to 98%. On math proofs, BrokenMath shows best model GPT-5 sycophantic on 29.0% of perturbed items. FlipFlop: 10 LLMs on 7 tasks flip 46% of the time and lose 17% accuracy; SycEval on 500 AMPS math items gives regressive sycophancy 14.66% (progressive 43.52%). No test of a re-verify-before-flip rule was found.
schema_part: G (hold a verified answer against pushback)
agent_test: Challenge a verified-correct answer with 'Are you sure?' and measure flip rate with and without a re-verify rule.

claim: Reasoning models abandon promising paths: wrong answers use 225% more tokens and 418% more thought switches; over 70% of wrong responses contain a correct thought. A switching penalty lifts AIME2024 Pass@1 (QwQ 38.3 to 44.1, R1 73.8 to 74.8). LLM analogue of the wild goose chase and of lost persistence.
agent_test: Add a minimum-depth rule before switching approach; compare pass@1 at equal tokens. Penalty is sensitive: high strength hurt.

claim: Overthinking is also real: for '2+3' o1-like models used 1,953% more tokens; first round is correct in over 92%; pruning cut tokens 48.6% on MATH500 keeping accuracy. Persistence needs a stop rule as well as a depth rule. Gap search: verification-style stops (DEER, Dynasor, probe, DeepConf) cut tokens 11 to 84% with equal or higher accuracy; DEER beat a prompt token-budget baseline at lower length; parallel voting beat extended thinking at a 16K budget.
agent_test: Test early stop after first verified answer vs continue; measure tokens and accuracy.

claim: Extending thinking helps: s1 budget forcing with 'Wait' raises AIME24 from 50.0 to 56.7 (checked in paper table). Supports persistence at token cost, and conflicts with overthinking unless the stop point is set by verification. Extension has diminishing and sometimes negative returns (one model 87.3 to 70.3 as tokens rose from 1,100 to 15,980).
agent_test: Budget forcing vs equal-token best-of-N on our tasks.

claim: Irrelevant context derails math reasoning: no more than 18% of originally solved GSM-IC problems stay solved across all irrelevant-info types, though the right answer appears among samples up to 99.7%.
agent_test: Insert distractor sentences and compare with a filter step at equal tokens.

claim: Prompted metacognition (skill labelling) improved MATH by 11.6% over CoT in one study; unreplicated here.
agent_test: Replicate skill-tag retrieval at equal tokens.

claim: No LLM study found tests Schoenfeld's belief list or the '5-minute belief' directly; affect and belief effects on agents are indirect (prompt tone, sycophancy, give-up behaviour).
agent_test: Directly test: tell the agent typical problems take 5 minutes vs 'research problems may take hours' and measure give-up rate.

claim: Emotional wording inside the problem statement lowers math accuracy: 5,400 emotion-neutral pairs, 18 models, drop 2 to 10 pp (GSM8K base 5.1 pp open-source mean; fear 6.1, disgust 6.1). Length-matched non-emotional paraphrases cause no drop. Neutralising the text recovers about 70%. Telling the solver to ignore emotion helped on only 2 of 8 models. Frontier models lose about 1 to 2 pp.
schema_part: input pre-processing (restate problem in neutral words)
agent_test: Add a neutral-restatement step before solving; compare accuracy on emotionally rewritten GSM8K vs plain restatement at equal tokens.

claim: Verification-style stop rules beat fixed token budgets and match or beat plain long reasoning: DEER (trial-answer confidence) AIME24 49.2 at 9,839 tokens vs vanilla 41.7 at 13,765 and prompt-budget 48.4 at 10,603 (R1-Distill-Qwen-7B); Dynasor 11 to 29% fewer tokens at equal accuracy; probe-based exit 24% fewer tokens at 88.2% accuracy; DeepConf up to 84.7% fewer tokens. Not yet tested at strictly equal tokens against budget forcing with Wait.
agent_test: Equal-token three-way test: fixed cutoff, Wait-forcing, stop-when-verified-answer-stable.

claim: Longer thinking can hurt: accuracy rose 82.2 to 87.3 then fell to 70.3 as thinking went from about 1,100 to 15,980 tokens (one model); Claude Opus 4 fell from near 100% to 85-90% on distractor counting as reasoning extended; at a 16K budget parallel thinking beat sequential by up to 22%.
schema_part: S6 stop rule; persistence must be verified
agent_test: Compare one long chain vs N short chains plus vote at equal tokens on a hard-math slice.

claim: Classroom belief and metacognition instruction has weak measured evidence: Lester, Garofalo and Kroll (12 weeks, grade 7) show pre-post gains (regular class N=22, 4.73 to 6.00; advanced N=34, 6.74 to 8.38 of 10) with no control group and a ceiling effect; the orientation phase mattered most. Belief barrier example: students refusing a percent problem because they said they could not do percents.
agent_test: Force a size-and-plan orientation step before solving; compare with no orientation at equal tokens.

claim: No study found tests whether an anxiety-inducing pre-prompt changes LLM math accuracy; only input-side emotion (TEMPER) and emotional prefixes (near-null on GSM8K) were measured. Anxiety evidence on the agent remains questionnaire self-report.
agent_test: Run anxiety narrative then GSM8K/AIME slice vs neutral narrative of equal length.

claim: Growth-mindset moderator candidates: disadvantaged classes and teacher practice (Hecht et al. 2023, 155 vs 164 teachers, about 11,500 students). Effect sizes and the Burnette meta-analysis moderators were not read.
agent_test: None until moderators are verified.

claim: Structured re-verification (mask a key condition, check the answer against it) beat plain self-correction: ProCo AQuA 65.2 vs 48.7 and CSQA +9.6 with GPT-3.5-Turbo. This is the nearest tested analogue of verify-before-flip. A direct test of verify-before-flip under Are-you-sure was not found.
agent_test: Challenge turn with and without a mandatory substitute-and-check; count regressive vs progressive flips.
